memory_update.text: SPSC should be tracked as a non-obvious retail supplier-compliance infrastructure candidate: the chokepoint is EDI/trading-partner workflow stickiness, not consumer brand demand.

SENEA is a strong underfollowed private-label/value-channel food supplier candidate because filings directly reference private label, mass merchandisers, limited-assortment stores, club stores, and dollar stores.

NEOG is a second-order compliance/testing candidate; survival in later layers requires evidence that food-safety testing volumes are tied to retailer audits or private-label supplier qualification rather than only broad food/animal diagnostics demand.

ODC is a speculative_shadow candidate for private-label household consumables through lightweight litter and co-pack/private-label exposure; later layers must verify customer/channel concentration and durability of co-pack growth.

TreeHouse Foods appears relevant to private-label food manufacturing but should be excluded from the US-listed universe unless current listing status is reverified; search evidence indicated a take-private transaction/private status.

For this node, durable bottlenecks may sit in retailer qualification workflows: EDI compliance, RFID/label compliance, food-safety testing, shelf-stable packaging, private-label manufacturing capacity, and co-pack execution.

node: Private-label and value-retail inputs: food, household goods, packaging, labels, and compliance
summary: Expanded the underfollowed lane around scarce retailer-qualified execution inputs rather than consumer-facing brands. The strongest Layer 1B candidates are mundane but operationally embedded suppliers: retail EDI/compliance infrastructure, private-label packaged food production, food-safety testing, and value-channel household/pet consumables. The chokepoint is not brand demand alone; it is the ability to meet retailer-specific specs, audits, EDI workflows, fill-rate requirements, food-safety standards, shelf-life constraints, and low-cost execution at scale.
